Frames — evidence, not decoration

Foundation already standing

Track spine
Legs-and-fillets centreline, exact closure, one surfaceAt() queried by everything, swept mesh from the same stations.
Vehicle
Four raycast wheels, spring and damper, grip circle, slip-gated drift charge in three tiers.
Collision
Barriers are half-planes in track space, so the clamp is an exact swept test at any speed.
Verification
Playwright harness driving the production build; named frames each stating what they prove.

Defects found by looking, not by reading

  • The cel shader multiplied by the light colour as well as the band level, darkening every surface by the ambient's own luminance.
  • Nothing converted linear to sRGB on output — the whole game rendered about five stops too dark.
  • The mesh builder's winding was inverted, so every generated box was inside-out and back-face culled. Karts rendered as solid black shells.
  • The Sobel's relative depth test fired across the entire road, because a grazing surface has a large depth gradient by construction.
  • A jump ramp launched at 31° for 102 m, clear over its landing. Caught by the validator's ballistic probe, not by eye.

What this page is not claiming

  • No side-by-side against Mario Kart 8 Deluxe is possible — the game is not available in this environment. The critic works from a written first-party rubric applied to our own captured frames.
  • Multiplayer is local split-screen. Online play needs an authoritative server, prediction and hosting, none of which exist here.
  • Frame timings come from a headless software rasteriser with no GPU. They bound the CPU cost only and say nothing about real device frame rate.
